What and why:
Microsoft recommends adopting a risk-based approach to Windows Server patching. It helps organizations respond faster to critical vulnerabilities while minimizing operational disruption. Rather than relying on fixed patching schedules, prioritize updates based on exploit activity, system exposure, workload criticality, and business impact.

Rollout schedule:
This guidance is available now.
 
Impact on your organization:
Organizations managing Windows Server workloads across on-premises, hybrid, and cloud environments can benefit from a risk-based patching strategy. The approach helps IT teams reduce security exposure, prioritize critical updates, and maintain service availability through appropriate testing and validation.
 
Action required/recommendations:
  • Assess risk: Maintain an inventory of servers, workloads, dependencies, and security exposure.
  • Define patching priorities: Establish routine, accelerated, and emergency response paths based on vulnerability risk.
  • Prepare for emergencies: Document and test deployment, validation, and rollback procedures.
  • Explore management tools: Use Azure Update Manager, Azure Arc, and supported Windows Server hotpatching capabilities to streamline updates.

Learn more: Building a risk-based patching response for Windows Server.
 
Compliance considerations:
Review your organization’s patching policies against applicable security and compliance requirements. Consider documenting risk-based patching timelines, approval processes, exceptions, compensating controls, and evidence of successful updates to support compliance and audit readiness.

Title: Building a risk-based patching response for Windows Server
